items.summary: Former Andhra Pradesh deputy chief minister and YSRCP leader Alla Kali Krishna Srinivas, popularly known as Alla Nani, died of a cardiac arrest in Visakhapatnam on Tuesday, September 15. He was 56. Alla Nani, who served as Health and Medical Education Minister in the YS Jagan Mohan Reddy government, was a three-time MLA from the Eluru Assembly constituency. His mortal remains were taken to his native Eluru by road, where family members, supporters and followers paid their last respects. Alla Nani reportedly went for a morning walk and returned home before complaining of uneasiness. He was rushed to a hospital after suffering a cardiac arrest but died during treatment. His body will be cremated in Eluru on Wednesday, September 16. He is survived by his wife Alla Rekha and two sons, Alla Kalikrishna Manichandra and Alla Ashish. Born on December 30, 1969, in Eluru in the erstwhile West Godavari district, Alla Nani was the son of Alla Suryachandra Rao and Nagamani. He completed his schooling at KP High School in Eluru in 1985 and his Intermediate education at Sir CR Reddy College in 1988. items.title: Karnataka HC upholds eviction of doctor from home over harassment of his 82-year-old mother
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has upheld the eviction of a government doctor from his residence after his 82-year-old mother alleged that he and his wife were harassing her and interfering with her peaceful life [ Dr. M S Mahesh v. Deputy Commissioner ]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj took note of Section 22 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007. Among other provisions, this Section calls on the State to to frame an action plan for the protection of life and property of senior citizens. The High Court held that the expression "protection of life and property of senior citizens” under Section 22 is wide enough to protect a senior citizen's enjoyment of her home. The Bench added that the statutory protection extends beyond the mere payment of maintenance and can include removing any source of harassment from a senior citizen's residence where the facts justify such action. “For a senior citizen, it carries with it the right to live with dignity, and that includes the right to reside peacefully in her own home without fear, harassment or humiliation,” the Court said in its August 6 order.
